item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there PhthaloType. Let's take a look at your concept.

One night that boredom is broken by strange occurrences among the specimens, and the team tries make sense of the situation while responding with limited resources and little support.

Hmm. Could you elaborate on this in a reply below? It's hard to gauge whether a Tale will work unless we have the specific details of what happens to whom, and when. Don't worry about spoiling me. Break down the major plot beats until the ending.

I'm glad that you're basing a narrative off an existing SCP - you'll be able to put your own unique spin on it, and like you said, lore-build. But I need to know the details of what happens before I can offer feedback (and a greenlight).

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I'll take another look. All the best!

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Typowriter: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Typowriter
item.content:encoded:
Goo Goo Gaa Gaa, Baby Crit Inbound

*Pulls out Baby Clipboard
Hold all my calls Baby Helen

I honestly can't be bothered to read an SCP rn, but from the part I skimmed, I don't see any reason why this guy would make an anomalous typewriter. Unless I'm missing something (which is a very real possibility), I don't see a connection. Also, if your going to link this to another SCP, remember to contact the author for permission once you get greenlit.

A big issue here is incident reports, changelogs, every bit of news the foundation produces is subject to this. Lets put that aside for now though. Why would the foundation keep this thing in range of a town? Why would they not just send it to a site in the middle of nowhere and prevent any incident?

The reality anchors do not work on this SCP, in actuality because it kills some of the fun associated with it.

No. Just. No. I may be a newbie here, but you can't just say the normal way of dealing with the anomaly just "doesn't work". SRAs are a staple of the SCP foundation, and unless you can find a in universe reason for why they don't work, people are going to lose immersion. A simple fix is the foundation keeps it in a storage locker with an SRA or 2 and takes it out for testing every once in a while.

I don't do recrits, so please don't PM me, thanks

Angryman, awaaaay

item.title: The Monster that Didn't Exist: The Monster that Didn't Exist
item.content:encoded:
A tale about SCP-3930, and what happened when something crawled out of it.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Standard (black highlighter theme to match SCP-3930's style)

Elevator Pitch: A tale of terror, paranoia, and suspense told from the terrified perspective of Dr Vasiliev as he desperately tries to figure out how to destroy this entity with minimal loss of life, all while distracted by a barely perceptible noise that is ringing in his ears.

+ Open Narrative +
- Close Narrative -

Central Narrative:
- Dr Vasiliev is monitoring SCP-39301 and notices a noise from the void, and something at its forefront. As he watches, the thing at its forefront drags itself out of the void and starts moving towards the Site
- Dr Vasiliev has just enough time to notify everyone on-Site that something is coming before it arrives
- The tale follows Dr Vasiliev as he runs and hides through the Site
- As he dismisses possible solutions, the tale's perspective switches between Dr Vasiliev (who is running and hiding) and various other scientists (who are running and are caught)
- When the scientists are caught, their perspective focuses on one of their five main senses and how the sense is distorted as they become a pattern screamer. Hearing is the only one not mentioned…
- Dr Vasiliev finds a radio and hears voices in the static that tell him there can be no more than ten, after which he tells everyone to gather in the cafeteria
- Dr Vasiliev counts 11 people and reluctantly notifies them that one of them has to die to stop the entity
- As they are having a discussion, the door where Dr Vasiliev and one other scientist are standing bursts open
- The perspective switches to the scientist next to Dr Vasilev as that scientist is attacked, focusing on hearing. However, the perspective switches back to Dr Vasiliev before things get weird
- As the scientist dies and the entity faces Dr Vasiliev, he realises the sound he's hearing is also coming from the entity
- The entity (and the sound) begins to slowly disappear, and as they do Dr Vasiliev realises what he's been hearing this whole time: the faintest, almost imperceptible sound of screaming

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The name of the article (and probably the article this tale is associated with) would draw the reader's attention, and the subject (scientists hunted by the unfathomable) would also hook the reader in.

Additional Notes: None

That's it for now. Thanks for reading, and hopefully this is intriguing!
P.S I don't want this to be (nor do I think it is) a cheap attempt to gain popularity by riding the coattails of a popular article, I simply wanted to write a tale about the 'something' that crawled out of the void. It would be nice to know if this seems like it though.

Footnotes
1. It wasn't called that back then, but I'm still thinking of a name.

item.title: Nostalgic House. Seeking Greenlights.: Nostalgic House. Seeking Greenlights.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A house with various anomalous properties. To say a few:

+ show block
– hide block

The house always bears the appearance of the viewer's childhood home, but will be in poor condition, as if it is many decades old. If multiple subjects view the house at once, it will stay resemblant of the first viewer's childhood home. Entities inside also behave this way.

The inside of the house1 consists of hallways, large rooms, staircases both up and down, and [DATA EXPUNGED].

As some subjects travel farther through SCP-XXXX-1, their features will become more like those of a child; they will become shorter, and their behaviour and patterns of speech will become more childlike. Most of those affected by this had bad childhoods.

Once the subject travels an unknown distance, they will encounter a room identical to the subject's childhood nursery. Upon entering the 'nursery', the subject will see visions of themselves between the ages of 2 and 8, playing by themselves or with a parent. After approximately 30 seconds of visual contact with the inside of the room, the vision of themselves will vanish. At this point, an entity known as SCP-XXXX-22 will approach the subject and tap them on the shoulder. Once the subject turns around, SCP-XXXX-2 will close the door to the room. SCP-XXXX-2 and the subject will both vanish. Recovering them is impossible. This only happens if the subject is alone.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is discovered by Dr. Mary Turner, an Assistant Researcher at Site-17, on break. She reported its existence to Site Command, which resulted in them sending MTF Phi-7 "Home Improvement" inside. They find an SCP-XXXX-33 instance in the form of a dog. It attacks one of their agents. The rest of the agents retreat. Later, Dr. Turner is assigned to SCP-XXXX. A month later, SCP-XXXX-2 breaches containment. During the breach, SCP-XXXX-2 locks itself in a room with Dr. █████ ███████ and disappears with her, later remanifesting inside SCP-XXXX-1. Dr. ███████ was never recovered. Dr. Turner proposes the reclassification of SCP-XXXX as Euclid. SCP-XXXX-2 ceases to attempt breaching containment, so SCP-XXXX stays Safe classified.

Hook: It's a creepy nostalgic childhood home with a reality-bending butler. It's not every day you go on the wiki and find one of those.

Additional Notes: Alright, so I'm trying to make a memetic hazard house that turns people into kids and has a reality-bending parent. Did I do it right?

Footnotes
1. Designated SCP-XXXX-1.
2. A humanoid entity 2.5 meters in height, also known as The Lost Parent.
3. Entities that take form of subject's childhood pets and toys. They either attack or be affectionate.

item.title: Seeking greenlights: Seeking greenlights
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional/ exploration

Elevator Pitch: What happens when you put a space in between the past, and the present? This is the basis of Liminal spaces and what this SCP is based on. So what happens when you put someone in a dimension of nothing but liminal spaces? How would they affect someone and what if they could spread if they weren't monitored?

Central Narrative: The central narrative of this SCP to show liminal spaces activate memories and experiences we have never had, SCP-XXXX is a rotting wooden door attached to a concrete floor and concrete wall that has been ripped out of its original place, the inside being bigger than it's exterior. The inside contains a series of endless hallways with wooden doors lining each wall that lead deeper into SCP-XXXX with entryways to the next hallway every 10 miles. Each door that has never been unopened before leads to a completely random room correlating to the subject's suppressed memories, intentions, and or emotions, often being broken in ways like repeating sections or missing areas entirely, or random items in said rooms. The door must always stay closed for it is opened and consistently stayed open for longer than 20 minutes, the warped reality will spread to everything, including organic matter, concrete is found to be the least affected by this property. Exposure longer than 4 hours leads to a steady loss of direction.
So, what happens when someone is put inside for long periods of time? This is about a D class being put into SCP-XXXX for longer than a week. This leads to the D class to end up remembering who he is, his real name, and just why he was put on death row and forced to be a test subject in the foundation. This leads to acceptance of his actions, knowing that the foundation will mostly cut him off for retaining this information, he must come to terms knowing that he will either never make it out of here, or be killed by the foundation.

hook/Attention-Grabber: These spaces have popped up on the internet all over, oftentimes people saying it feels oddly familiar with an overwhelming sense of deja vu. This SCP takes this idea of Liminal Spaces and turns it into an endless expanse of repeating rooms and endless, useless mazes of warped reality and turns it into an eerie dimension of random exploration.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP and I am bound to make mistakes as an inexperienced Author, be as harsh or factual as you need. I want to do an SCP right.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Keep Him In The Dark: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Keep Him In The Dark
item.content:encoded:
Called by PM

+ show block
– hide block

So my concern here is that you’ve written yourself into a corner. SCP travels between dimensions, but doesn’t know. He can’t know. And in all of those dimensions he’s contained by the foundation.

The first thing I’d say is if the multiple foundation variants are aware that he’s going from containment cell to containment cell and not really aware of it, they could just leave well enough alone. Why try to stop his shifting? As long as the containment protocols are in place, he wouldn’t be able to breach in a traditional sense at all.

Second thing, because he’s just flitting from one containment cell to the next, this isn’t the most exciting of ideas. You can’t do wild stories because his life is prettt much always the same. AND because he doesn’t know, you also can’t develop his feelings about the matter because part of the premise is he’s ignorant.

Finally, it sorta beggars belief that all seven foundations have information sharing to the point where they have parallel files on him that are updated accordingly.

All in all, this seems like a much dryer version of the Unwilling Dimension Hopper skip from early on…

Without a completely rewritten concept at its core, I don’t know that this article would survive as you propose it currently.

item.title: Crown of need (Seeking Greenlight): Crown of need (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An Euclid SCP (scp-xxx) that consists of an indestructible object (crown/trophy/statuette, i haven't decided yet) that has the ability teleport between any of two persons (hosts), upon the receiving host performing a specific ritual. Scp-xxx will also, trough unknown methods, transfer a seemingly random amount of money from the sender host to the receiver.

  • list item

Scp-xxx's ritual description can be relatively easily found in the internet, usually in the form of ads, like: "MAKE A LOT OF MONEY WITH ONE WEIRD METHOD". It is unknown if these ads are generated by scp-xxx or another party.

  • list item

The ritual will change after the hosts rotate.

  • list item

People with low income tend to have more brand losses as sender hosts, but this is not reliable enough to make predictions

Central Narrative:
The article will consist of research logs of the foundation trying to determine what dictates the amount of money that is transferred. The foundation will treat these research with a distinct urgency, that's because scp-xxx will withdraw copious amounts of money from the foundation while in its custody, between 5 - 50 million (i'm open to sugestions regarding this) generally a week after its containment.

Taking in account the worrying financial damage the foundation is undertaking while trying to contain scp-xxx, a deadline to cease scp-xxx containment has been set to avoid the foundation going bankrupt.

One foundation researcher was able to produce 100$, unfortunately the researched died in an unrelated accident. Since then, more hosts are being used to determine what caused this drop in transferred money .

Eventually the foundation found a D-class personnel refugy from [REDACTED] that produced a similar amount of money.

The rest will be available at the final draft.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
This should be an interesting scp since it poses more of a practical instead of being outright harmful to people.

Additional Notes:
English is not my main language, so i might need extra help in grammar stuff

item.title: A Deconstruction of the Foundations Modus Operandi (SCP): Re: A Deconstruction of the Foundations Modus Operandi (SCP)
item.content:encoded:
Well, I guess you could call it a zombie plague, but I suppose it's more nuanced than that. I mean, the infected aren't undead or anything; they'll die just as easy as any other human. Moreover, it'll be written in such a way to make it interesting. For instance, it is implied the phenomenon manifested due to the lynching of the poor Jewish gentlemen, who was repeatedly burned as a form of torture. The reason why the infection can only be destroyed through incineration is because those that killed Parisian Man used fire to burn him, even though he wasn't infected. This triggered some kind of anomalous event, fuelled by the victims hate. The murderers would've succumb to the very plague they accused him of causing, with the only escape being death through fire (coincidently, the same way they killed him.)

Moreover, not to bash 008 (it was a product of its time), but mine will go into more detail about the anomalous disease. For instance, the researchers find the bacteria lacks efflux pumps, drug-inactivating enzymes, or any other mechanism known to confer resistance to antibiotics. Despite this, antibiotics have no effect whatsoever. The minutiae may not be for everyone, but I like writing with a heavily scientific tone, sort of like an academic research paper.

+ show block
– hide block

Frankly, I don't think it's even necessary for you to write an SCP if this story is
all you'll be focusing on - you could just write it in as a tale around 1609. But
then again, that's completely up to you.

The SCP will be interesting in and of itself (ideally, anyway). The 1609 realisation is just kind of an oh shit ending I want to wrap it. Moreover, by writing a tale, it'd be difficult to explore the characterisation of Miller. The repeated neutralisation denials are what drive him to ask "Why are the Foundation so adamant on containing anomalies we can't learn anything from, even when they're dangerous? Is it because we're afraid of unintended consequences, or do the O5s have their own agenda?"

How exactly does Miller find out about the conspiracy? Everything in the
Foundation is under lock, key and blast gate when it comes to any sort of
administration - let alone the O5.

So, Miller actually has Level 4 Access (justified, in my opinion, because he's working with an anomaly that could theoretically cause an XK-Class End-of-the-World Scenario.) That being said, he obviously doesn't have access to the O5 councils dirty little secrets. The way in which he finds out is as follows:

Miller is actually a GOC mole, trying to change the Foundation from the inside. By conferring with contacts within the GOC, he finds out that the supposed 1609 event never happened, and there's no record of the people that supposedly died ever existing. In fact, the GOC had never even heard of 1609. From that, Miller pieces the rest together. This would leave the reader wondering who to believe. Are the GOC lying to Miller, or are the Foundation lying and using fictional botched neutralisation attempts as a form of propaganda?

(This is subject to change, but the most believable way in which I could justify Miller working it out. Nobody wants a terrible cliche in which he just magically hacks the database)

Why kill Miller ala FBI/FSB if they can just amnesticize him or change his memories?
It's simple, quiet and cheap. More so than staging a breach is, at any rate.

They kill him because he's a mole. Obviously, they can't just make a Level 4 project lead disappear because people would ask questions. They can't be honest either, because they don't want people to know the Foundation was infiltrated. Therefore they orchestrate a controlled containment breach, and order Beta-7 to kill everyone within the quarantine zone (which, conveniently, includes Miller).

How are you planning to convey the whole story? I'm assuming you're going to
write a different format after the article - no way is O5 letting a story like that be
featured in one.

Everything up to the breach log can be accessed normally. The breach log ends with Miller typing something on his terminal when Beta-7 breach his office and shoot him. The final file will be behind level 5 access. So you go through the rigamarole of Level 5 Classified Warnings etcetera etcetera, there's mention of a memetic kill agent, then the file opens with "Welcome, Overseer." Therefore, it's sort of implied the reader is a member of the O5 Council in this scenario. The contents of the final file are what Miller was writing on his terminal, detailing the shady stuff the O5's are doing, how 1609 doesn't actually exist etc. It's implied he was going to try to send this information to the GOC before he was killed.

So yeah, that will be the end. Hopefully it'll leave the reader wondering who was telling the truth, the Foundation or the GOC. I want to leave the reader questioning the Foundations obsession with containing everything, rather than outright destroying anomalies that pose a threat to humanity.

item.title: The Abyss is Safe (seeking Crits and Greenlight): Re: The Abyss is Safe (seeking Crits and Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

The narrative is centered on how the foundation sets up a provisional site at the bottom of the ocean to observe and study this space, for the purpose of research, making sure other deep sea expeditions don't discover it, and to insure the stranger organisms not resembling common ocean life don't accidently drift out and become a problem.

This seems more like a small paragraph in the description or conprocs, than a narrative.

When on of the older cremates dies due to deteriorating health both mentally and physically, the others only option is a 'burial at sea'. Of course, as cruel as the Foundation can be, they haven't killed someone and tossed the body into an ocean that preserves life, which ends up happening when the body left out on the rocky sea floor is pulled into the entrance.

Why is this the only option? Why not transport it to the surface and then dispose? This seems incredibly short sighted and stupid of a foundation team specifically going to the bottom of the Ocean to study a magic portal to another ocean, that would preserve life… to then "bury at sea"

leaving it to the next crew to investigate, hinting that this could all happen again.

Like, what is going to "happen again"? Someone is gonna die down there and get buried at sea? that seems unlikely as hell… ALSO what is the ramifications of this action?


Ultimately, this idea seems rather convoluted to get to a vague ethical dilemma. Why is this portal at the bottom of the ocean but leads to another ocean, that makes you "immortal" sorta? Like it just seems like so many layers to get to "should we have been more careful with this body?"
